routeAdvice.decision: NO-GO as the route-advice adapter today
reasons: STRUCTURAL MISFIT (verifier-confirmed against core_concepts.md): a Switchyard Target is 'one upstream model ID + client', fixed in routes.toml at deploy time; all seven routing algorithms (passthrough, random, LLM-classifier, stage, escalation, complexity, custom) select among pre-configured targets. There is NO API to rank an arbitrary caller-supplied candidate list — which is the cockpit's hard requirement (ARCHITECTURE.md:70 scopes the adapter to re-ranking already-eligible candidates).

MATURITY (confidence 0.85, adversarially confirmed): v0.2.0 (2026-08-10, latest as of 2026-09-01) says 'remains pre-alpha software'; the reference server README says 'Demo server, not for production use' verbatim. Partner names (LangChain, Kong, Boomi, Cognition) are evaluators/integrators, not GA proof.

BENCHMARK CAVEATS: the attractive staged-escalation numbers (LangChain 74% cost cut at ~93% accuracy retention; Cognition/Devin 28% cheaper near-frontier) are self-reported by NVIDIA+partners and used a superseded frontier baseline (Opus 4.8, two weeks after Opus 5 shipped).
Distinct from NVIDIA's older 'LLM Router' Blueprint (config.yaml, single-pick classifier, no ranked scores) — also a no-go for this seam.
revisitWhen: an API accepts per-request candidate lists or returns ranked scores over caller-supplied models

alternativesAssessed.not-diamond: Only router whose API is designed around caller-supplied candidate lists + eval scores (closest contract fit), but ranked last (12/12) on RouterArena's independent quality board and over-selects expensive models.
alternativesAssessed.routellm: OSS, self-hostable, but binary strong/weak only (not N-way ranking) and flagged for embedding-API latency.
